paragraphs: Avdan is Abba Yudan (Tosafot, Yevamot 105b: Avdan is a shortened form), Rabbi’s student. He was afflicted with leprosy and his two sons drowned because he spoke against Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose (see there). He was a great and pious sage. In the rulings on Berakhot, chapter Tefillat Hashachar, in the Jerusalem Talmud’s name (mishnah 1: Rabbi instructed Avdon the interpreter): he was Rabbi’s interpreter. He asked Rabbi how many degrees apply to sacred food and terumah (Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter 5 of Berakhot). Avidan said, “Once the skies became overcast,” etc., and they asked Rabbi, Berakhot 27b. Rabbi told him (Niddah 66a). Rabbi sat expounding and said to Abba Yudan his interpreter, “Announce to the congregation”; Bereshit Rabbah, section 10.
